source: Martin & Schwartz (2005) Physically distributed learning, Cognitive Science 29
finding: Five studies with 9-10 year olds on fractions. Handling physical pieces helped children build an interpretation. Children who already understood re-arranged the setting; children still learning copied its given structure. Children who adapted loosely structured settings transferred better than children given well-structured ones.
numbers: Abstract-level only (Crossref text); per-study N and effect sizes not read.
quote: the opportunity to adapt an environment permits the development of new interpretations that can advance learning
limits: Full text blocked (Wiley challenge page). Small child samples. The claim is about new interpretations, not reduced load.
agent_relevance: Design lesson: an environment helps when the agent can re-shape it, not only read it. Give the agent a workspace it can rearrange (files, test harness), not a fixed template.

source: Trninic, Kapur & Sinha (2020) The disappearing 'Advantage of Abstract Examples in Learning Math'
finding: Critical replication of Kaminski, Sloutsky and Heckler (2008, Science), which claimed abstract examples beat concrete ones for transfer. With better-designed concrete examples, concrete training did as well as or better than abstract training.
numbers: Abstract only; N and statistics not read.
limits: Concerns concreteness, not embedding. Shows a famous 'concrete is worse' result depended on weak concrete examples.
agent_relevance: A negative result for situated material can come from poor material. When testing 'environment help' for our agent, make the environment condition as good as the control.

source: Boettger, Poschik & Zierer (2023) Does the Brain Drain Effect Really Exist? A Meta-Analysis, Behav Sci 13(9):751
finding: Meta-analysis of whether a smartphone nearby or in use harms cognition (an environment that taxes the mind). Overall effect small and negative, high heterogeneity, and only memory reached significance.
numbers: 22 studies, 43 effects. Overall |g| = 0.14 (CI 0.03 to 0.24), Q(42)=110.06, I2=61.8%. Memory |g|=0.23 (CI 0.10 to 0.36, p<.001). Attention |g|=0.07 (p=.29). General cognition |g|=0.10 (p=.76). Asia |g|=0.39 (p<.001); Europe 0.20 (p=.12); North America 0.03 (p=.60). Signs were lost in my text extraction; the paper reports them negative.
limits: Mixed use and presence studies; heterogeneity unexplained; small subgroups.
agent_relevance: The cost of a distracting environment is small and not universal. Measure per task type; memory tasks are most sensitive.

source: Ward, Duke, Gneezy & Bos (2017) Brain drain: mere presence of one's smartphone reduces cognitive capacity (original; not opened)
finding: Original claim: a phone on the desk lowered working-memory capacity and fluid intelligence versus a phone in another room. Recalled from the literature, not read this session.
numbers: About 520 undergraduates in Exp 1, three phone locations. Unverified.
limits: Not opened. Included because b03 and b05 test it.
agent_relevance: Context left in view may cost capacity, but b03 shows the pooled cost is small.

source: Reexamining the 'brain drain' effect: a replication of Ward et al. (2017), Acta Psychologica 2022
finding: A replication of Ward et al. exists (found via OpenAlex, 21 citations). The page returned 403, so I did not read the result.
numbers: Not read.
limits: Do not use this line for numbers. It marks where to look next.
agent_relevance: Check it before using brain-drain as design evidence.

source: Google effects on memory: a meta-analytical review of intensive Internet search, Front Public Health (2024)
finding: Random-effects meta-analysis of the Google effect (people remember less of what they expect to look up). Pooled effect reported as moderate and significant but with very wide intervals; region was the only significant moderator.
numbers: 879 records, 69 full texts, 22 studies. Pooled |d| about 1.01 (CI 0.12 to 2.13). Europe |d|=1.11, North America 1.04. Cognitive self-esteem |d|=0.53; psychophysiology 0.13 (CI spans zero). Bias checked by funnel plot only; no trim-and-fill.
limits: Very wide CIs; mixed outcome types; a size of d near 1 for a media effect is suspicious. Authors admit bias not fully tested.
agent_relevance: Offloading shifts storage toward where to find things. For an agent, store location and key, not full content, when the store is reliable.

source: Camerer et al. (2018) Evaluating the replicability of social science experiments in Nature and Science 2010-2015
finding: 21 high-profile experiments replicated with samples about 5 times larger. 13 (62%) replicated in the same direction; mean replicated effect about half the original. Sparrow et al. (2011) Google effects on memory was among the set; I recall it did not replicate but could not open the paper to confirm.
numbers: 13 of 21 (62%); effect about 50% of original (search summary only). Sparrow outcome unverified.
limits: Paywalled; search summary only.
agent_relevance: The founding offloading-and-memory finding is weaker than its fame. Prefer designs tested by code, not by the human-memory story.

source: Gilbert-lab line: Framing cognitive offloading in terms of gains or losses, Cognitive Research (2022)
finding: People use external reminders more than is optimal (reminder bias), most when underconfident in memory. Framing reminders as losses reduced the bias and raised willingness to rely on memory; gain framing kept it. Money incentives and confidence feedback in earlier work only partly fixed it.
numbers: Exp 1 N=141 after exclusions (between-subjects framing). Exp 2 within-subject; forced-internal accuracy about two thirds, forced-external near all; condition effect F(1,299)=991.36, partial eta2=0.77.
limits: Student and online samples; lab reminder task, not real work.
agent_relevance: People offload too eagerly when unsure. An agent may call a tool when its own answer would do; add a cost-aware rule for when to use the tool.

source: Wei et al. (2022) Chain-of-thought prompting elicits reasoning in large language models
finding: Writing intermediate steps is an external workspace for a model. PaLM 540B with 8 exemplars set state of the art on GSM8K. Many wrong chains were nearly right: slips such as calculator error, symbol mapping, a missing step.
numbers: 46% of inspected incorrect chains were nearly correct (minor slips); 54% had major semantic or coherence errors.
limits: Gain appears only at large scale.
agent_relevance: Written steps are scratch space, but arithmetic slips remain, so pair it with a real calculator or code run (b11).

source: Nye et al. (2021) Show Your Work: Scratchpads for intermediate computation with language models
finding: Models trained to write intermediate steps learned long addition; models without the scratchpad failed even at the largest size. On 9- and 10-digit addition (training used 1-8 digits) models without scratchpad completely failed; with scratchpad they improved with size.
numbers: Train 1-8 digits, 100k examples, 5k steps, batch 32; 10k in-distribution test, 1k per out-of-distribution length; sizes 2M to 1B parameters.
limits: Fine-tuned small transformers on synthetic tasks, not prompting a general model.
agent_relevance: Machine analogue of load reduction by an external workspace: it lifts the ceiling and generalises past training length.

source: Gao et al. (2022) PAL: Program-aided Language Models
finding: Moving the calculation out of the model into a Python interpreter beat chain-of-thought. The gain is large when numbers are large, where in-head arithmetic breaks.
numbers: GSM8K: PAL (Codex) 72.0% vs PaLM-540B CoT about 15 points lower (abstract: +15% absolute). GSM-Hard: CoT falls 65.6% to 20.1% (about -70% relative); DIRECT 19.7% to 5.0% (-74%); PAL stays at 61.5%. PAL averaged over 3 runs.
limits: Needs a problem expressible as code; Codex vs PaLM mixes model families; GSM-Hard built by the authors.
agent_relevance: Strongest evidence that moving a step from the head to the environment helps. Supports rule that code does counting.

source: Schick et al. (2023) Toolformer: Language models can teach themselves to use tools
finding: Letting a 6.7B model call a calculator, search and other APIs lifted zero-shot math sharply versus the same model with tools switched off. Skill lives with the tool.
numbers: ASDiv / SVAMP / MAWPS: GPT-J 7.5 / 5.2 / 9.9; Toolformer tools disabled 14.8 / 6.3 / 15.0; Toolformer with tools 40.4 / 29.4 / 44.0.
limits: Table text was garbled in PDF extraction; row order inferred. Tools used only when the model chose them.
agent_relevance: Same size model gains about 25 points from a tool. A tool is worth more than parameters on exact tasks. Removing the tool removes the gain (extended-versus-embedded test).

source: Yao et al. (2023) ReAct: Synergizing reasoning and acting in language models
finding: Interleaving thoughts with actions on an environment beat acting alone and beat imitation and RL baselines. Without thoughts the agent lost track of state and failed to break goals into subgoals.
numbers: ALFWorld: best ReAct trial 71% vs best Act 45% vs BUTLER 37%; worst ReAct trial 48% beat both; relative gain over Act 33% to 90%, mean 62% over six trials. ReAct-IM 53 vs ReAct 71 overall. WebShop: +10% absolute over previous best. HotpotQA EM: Standard 27.1, CoT 28.9, ReAct 33.8.
limits: Hand-written few-shot prompts; 500-question HotpotQA sample; few trials.
agent_relevance: Reasoning plus environment feedback beats either alone. Matches the schema: act, observe real output, then reason from it.

source: Yang et al. (2024) SWE-agent: Agent-Computer Interfaces enable automated software engineering
finding: Same model, different interface to the computer, different success. Editing with a linter, a bounded file viewer and summarised search raised SWE-bench Lite results; iterative search that tempted exhaustive scrolling did worse than no search tool.
numbers: SWE-bench Lite (300): edit with linting 18.0 vs edit without 15.0; no edit tool 10.3; summarised search 18.0 vs no search 15.7 vs iterative search 12.0; viewer 100 lines 18.0 vs 30 lines 14.3 vs full file 12.7. 1,185 of 2,294 trajectories (51.7%) had a failed edit; recovery odds fall as failed edits accumulate.
limits: Ablations on 300 instances, one model; run-to-run noise of a few points.
agent_relevance: Environment design is the lever: interface and feedback format matter as much as the prompt. More options can hurt.

source: Huang et al. (2024) Large language models cannot self-correct reasoning yet (ICLR)
finding: Without outside feedback, asking a model to revise its answer does not help and often hurts. Earlier gains came from oracle labels that told the model when it was wrong.
numbers: GPT-3.5 standard GSM8K / CommonSenseQA / HotpotQA 75.9 / 75.8 / 26.0; with oracle labels 84.3 / 89.7 / 29.0; intrinsic self-correction round 1: 75.1 / 38.1 / 25.0; round 2: 74.7 / 41.8 / 25.0. GPT-4 standard 95.5 / 82.0 / 49.0; oracle 97.5 / 85.5 / 59.0; intrinsic round 1: 91.5 / 79.5 / 49.0; round 2: 89.0 / 80.0 / 43.0.
limits: Row assignment inferred from garbled PDF table; few benchmarks.
agent_relevance: The environment must supply the signal. Rule G2 (revise only from real output) is supported: self-critique alone is not an environment.

source: Wang et al. (2023) Voyager: an open-ended embodied agent with large language models
finding: Minecraft agent driven by environment feedback, execution errors and a stored skill library. Removing parts hurt, most of all the curriculum and self-verification.
numbers: 3.3x more unique items, 2.3x longer distances, milestones up to 15.3x faster (wooden 15.3x, stone 8.5x, iron 6.4x). Ablations: random curriculum -93% items; no self-verification -73% items; no skill library plateaus.
limits: Single game; GPT-4 needed for code; no CIs in the text read.
agent_relevance: A library of verified skills is part of the environment, not the prompt. Fits the schema's stored checked results.

source: Cemri et al. (2025) Why do multi-agent LLM systems fail? (MAST)
finding: The social setting for LLMs (many agents) often does not reduce load. Failures cluster into specification and design issues, inter-agent misalignment and weak task verification. Adding verification helped.
numbers: 1600+ annotated traces; 14 failure modes in 3 categories; human agreement kappa 0.88; LLM annotator kappa 0.77; ChatDev on ProgramDev +15.6% from a high-level objective verification step; prompt-level fix +9.4%.
limits: Frameworks and models vary; shares come from selected systems.
agent_relevance: Social structure helps only with external verification. Matches G4: agents from one model are not independent checkers.

source: Kosmyna et al. (2025) Your Brain on ChatGPT: accumulation of cognitive debt
finding: Essay writing with an LLM, a search engine or no tool. LLM users showed weaker recall of what they wrote and low ownership. Use of the LLM impaired producing a correct quote from one's own essay.
numbers: 54 participants, 18 per group; 18 completed session 4. 15 of 18 (83.3%) LLM users failed to quote correctly vs 2 of 18 (11.1%) in both search and brain-only groups (p<.001 each vs LLM; search vs brain-only p=1.0).
limits: Small N, preprint, essay task; EEG claims not examined here.
agent_relevance: Offloading to an LLM costs memory of the output. For our agent: keep a program-readable record, since the model will not remember its own work.

source: Morehead, Dunlosky & Rawson (2019) and Urry et al. (2020): replications of Mueller & Oppenheimer (2014) laptop vs longhand notes
finding: Secondary summaries say the handwriting advantage largely failed to replicate: the 2019 replication reportedly found a small factual effect and no reliable conceptual gain; Urry et al. found no laptop disadvantage. Not verified.
numbers: d=0.45 factual and d=0.13 conceptual come from one secondary source and are unconfirmed; Urry exploratory meta-analysis of 8 studies reportedly agrees.
limits: Both papers paywalled or blocked; numbers unconfirmed.
agent_relevance: A popular 'medium of external notes matters' claim shrank under replication. Treat medium effects as small until measured.

source: Fyfe, McNeil, Son & Goldstone (2014) concreteness fading; Carbonneau et al. (2013) manipulatives meta-analysis (not retrieved)
finding: Not retrieved. The literature on physical manipulatives is generally reported as showing a small to moderate benefit that depends on guidance and on fading from concrete to abstract. Not verified here.
numbers: none verified
limits: Not opened.
agent_relevance: If the schema adds an environment, plan to fade it as checks pass, to avoid dependence.

source: Wheeler (2013) Is cognition embedded or extended? (rival-theory contrast; not opened)
finding: Embedded view: the environment scaffolds an inner process. Extended view: the environment is part of the process. They differ on whether the inner skill survives removal of the aid. Not read.
numbers: none
limits: Not opened; conceptual.
agent_relevance: Test for our agent: after removing a tool, does the gain stay? That separates crutch from part.

source: Hutchins (1995, 1996) Cognition in the Wild; via SEP (not opened)
finding: Ship navigation team: the computation is spread over people, charts and instruments. Founding ethnographic case; no controlled comparison or replication.
numbers: None (ethnographic).
limits: Qualitative; no comparison condition.
agent_relevance: Frames the idea, gives no measured gain. Keep out of the evidence-strength counts.

source: Gap check across sources read: no direct LLM test of 'environment reduces load'
finding: SWE-agent, PAL, ReAct and Voyager show that environment and tool design change results. None measures load, and none holds the tool fixed while varying only whether the agent may re-shape its workspace, which is Martin and Schwartz's key manipulation.
numbers: None.
limits: Inference from the sources I opened; absence of evidence, not proof.
agent_relevance: An experiment we could run: fixed tool, vary whether the agent may restructure its scratch files.

source: Huang et al. (2024) self-correction analysis, Section 3
finding: After two rounds of self-correction on GSM8K the model keeps its first answer most of the time, and among the changes it more often turns a right answer wrong than a wrong answer right. The authors say the model cannot judge its own reasoning.
numbers: GPT-3.5 GSM8K: retains initial answer 74.7% of the time.
limits: One model family and three benchmarks.
agent_relevance: Supports no self-judging step: the check must be code or real output.
quote: LLMs cannot properly judge the correctness of their reasoning.

source: Yang et al. (2024) SWE-agent, portability claim
finding: An interface built for GPT-4 Turbo also helped a different model, so part of the gain belongs to the environment, not to the one model.
numbers: SWE-agent with Claude 3 Opus solves 10.5% of SWE-bench; with GPT-4 Turbo 12.5% (abstract).
limits: Two models only; lower than GPT-4 Turbo, so tuning to one model still matters.
agent_relevance: A well-designed workspace transfers across models; build the harness once.
